title: Wasserstein Distance Drift: Calibration and Alarm Thresholds
content:
## What is Wasserstein Distance?
Wasserstein distance (also called Earth Mover's Distance) measures the minimum cost of transforming one probability distribution into another. Unlike KL-divergence, it is symmetric and well-defined even when distributions have non-overlapping support.

## Probe Alarm Thresholds
Probe uses the following calibrated thresholds for continuous features:

| Feature Type      | Low      | Medium   | High     | Critical |
|-------------------|----------|----------|----------|----------|
| Continuous (norm) | < 0.05   | 0.05–0.15| 0.15–0.30| > 0.30   |
| Continuous (skew) | < 0.10   | 0.10–0.25| 0.25–0.45| > 0.45   |
| Embedding (dense) | < 0.08   | 0.08–0.20| 0.20–0.35| > 0.35   |

## How Probe Computes Wasserstein
1. Reference window: last N samples before model training cutoff
2. Production window: last M samples from live serving
3. Wasserstein-1 computed per feature dimension
4. Aggregate score: weighted mean by feature importance from training

## Interpretation Guide
- Score near 0: Production distribution matches training closely.
- Score 0.15–0.25: Moderate shift. Check if it correlates with known business events.
- Score > 0.30: Significant transformation. Validate model assumptions are still valid.
- Score > 0.50: Distribution has fundamentally changed. Model likely invalid.

## Wasserstein vs PSI vs ADWIN
| Metric      | Strength | Weakness |
|-------------|----------|----------|
| Wasserstein | Sensitive to magnitude | Computationally intensive |
| PSI         | Simple to interpret | Insensitive to tail changes |
| ADWIN       | Online, real-time | Can be noisy on small windows |

Best practice: Use all three. ADWIN for real-time alerting, PSI for daily reports, Wasserstein for deep investigation.
